mark: Each mark is a small lantern: its colour glows up from the foot of the plate, the letters are in the serif, the round mark is a small sun, and the picked mark wears a halo (a ring held off the plate with a soft amber glow). Look for the glow at the foot, never a flat tint.
stackbar: The bar is a horizon: every part is lit at its foot, the 80 % limit is a small amber sun on a thin stalk, and the legend row you point at has the sun risen under it (an amber line along its foot with a warm wash). A sum past the whole ends in a ✳ instead of an arrow.
bullets: Titles and figures are in the serif. Pointing at a row lights its foot in amber with a warm wash and no underline. A warning or failing figure is the tone's light in its own ink on a faint wash from its foot, never a solid plate.
tick: A counting number stands overbright and warm, like first light, while it runs and cools into its ink when it lands. It never swells or jumps; watch the colour settle after the last digit.
uptime: A strip of days is a hillside lit from its foot: each cell keeps its fill and pattern and takes a faint light at the bottom. Pointing at a cell raises the sun under it (an amber foot line and a glow); the title and the percentage are in the serif.
uptime-states: Loading is the low sun's light crossing the strip from start to end, with the sun on its arc in the middle as the busy card. Empty and failed keep the exact footprint of the loaded strip; a failure reddens its own foot light instead of showing a red plate.
uptime-phone: The same strip at phone width: one line per strip, the serif title and the figures never touch, and the light still crosses while it loads.
inbox: Each row is a plate lit from its foot. Its state is the light on its start edge: amber for new, a cooler light for in flight, ochre for a warning, red for a failure; the next one up has the sun risen under it. What is done is quieter by ink, never faded. Titles are in the serif.
backlog: The same rows for a message backlog: lit from the foot, state shown by the light on the start edge, the serif for titles, buttons that are solstice's own with the sun rising under the pointer.
files: A list of files: the format sits in the lead column, the row's foot carries the faint light, and a failed file reddens its own sky. Buttons keep their columns and the busy press shows the sun on its arc.
appointments: The day and the hour are in the serif in the lead column; the next appointment has the sun risen under it (amber foot line and a warm wash) and past ones go quiet by ink, not by fading.
checks: A check with a reservation reddens its sky to ochre: the foot light and the mark are ochre, the detail is in the warning ink, and the written fix is a sentence in the serif. Failed rows keep the red sky.
sort: Nothing new is drawn here: the table keeps solstice's own head and sort marks. A column that cannot be sorted now is quieter and has no pointer, and the readout under it still names the sort.
kv: Keys are in the serif and sentence case, rows are separated by hairlines, a changed value gets a small glowing sun dot after its key, and a row that could not be read reddens its own foot light.
formrows: Labels are in the serif. A row changed and not saved has a lit strip on its start edge (amber, glowing); a row in error has the same strip in red. Lines between rows are hairlines.
tiles: Choice tiles are plates lit from their foot. Pointing raises the sun under a tile (amber foot line and a warm wash); the picked tile wears the halo: a ring held off the plate with a glow. A disabled tile is dashed and unlit.
card-states: A card in four states: its titles are in the serif, the loaded data rises into place when it returns, a failure reddens the card's own foot, and loading shows the sun on its arc in the busy card. All four keep the card's footprint.
header: The page header's title is in the serif; the mark, the badge and the freshness line sit on one line and never touch the title.
art: The empty-state drawings are the low sun on a horizon: none is the sun half up, nomatch an empty arc with a hollow ring, error a reddened sky, offline a broken arc, done the full sun, locked the sun behind a shutter. Each stroke rises from the horizon on a smooth sine, the sun first.
pipeline: Lanes and cards are plates lit from their foot in the stage's own colour; names and counts are in the serif; pointing at a card raises the sun under it, the open card wears the halo, and the marks are small glowing suns.
pipeline-states: Loading shows the sun on its arc over the board; an empty or failed board has its sentence on a plate lit from its foot, red when it failed, and the lanes keep their places.
journey: The journey is the sun's path: the rule between reached steps runs from rust to amber, reached steps are amber discs, and the step it stands at is a bigger sun with a halo. Names are in the serif.
journey-states: A closed journey ends in red: its last rule is dashed red and its mark glows red. Loading and empty keep the footprint of the loaded journey.
contact: Moments on the dated line are small suns with a glow in their kind's colour; a stretch is a hillside lit from its foot; pointing at a moment gives it a double amber ring.
contact-states: Empty and failed keep the room of the loaded line; the sentence sits on a plate, loading shows the busy card with the sun on its arc.
secret: The value box is lit from its foot. When it is shown the value rises into its line from below, and its time running out is a rule from rust to amber with the sun at its head, which sets at the end. A failure is the red sky.
secret-phone: The same field at phone width: the buttons go under the value, the line under keeps its room, and nothing touches.
manage: The dialog in sections: sections are divided by the horizon with one rust peak in its middle, headings are in the serif, and the danger section reddens its own sky (a red wash from its foot with a red line).
confirm: The confirmation lists what still uses the thing in a plate lit from its foot; a blocked removal shows no field and says why.
type-dialog: The typed confirmation: the list of what will be lost sits on a red-skied plate, the name to type is a chip with an amber foot line, and the match line is always there.
type-own: The same typed block in a page's own dialog: identical parts, the field's foot turns amber when the name matches.
type-phone: The typed confirmation at phone width: list, name, field and match line stack and nothing touches.
disc: The visual timer is a sky: the sector is the sun still above the horizon with a warm glow, the hub a small sun, the face lit from its foot, the name in the serif.
disc-states: Paused dims the sun; when the time is out the last light comes once, overbright, and cools (no endless breathing), and the face keeps a halo.
disc-phone: Three discs at phone width: the face shrinks to fit, the name and the line under it stay on one line each.
countdown: Countdown cards are lit from their foot with the digits in the serif; the colon and the digits keep their width so nothing moves while counting.
countdown-states: Paused mutes the digits; when time is up the card gets one overbright flare that cools, then keeps a halo and the amber digits.
range: The preset chips are solstice's segmented control; Custom wears the halo while it is open, the panel is the usual kindled popover, and the line under the bar is in the serif.
range-states: A wrong custom range reddens the field's foot and names the fault in a line that keeps its room; the panel and its buttons are solstice's own.
wheel: The wheel is a day turning: soft segments in the theme's colours between a glowing amber rim, a sun-coloured pointer, an amber hub. It settles smoothly on the sine's last quarter, and the outcome name is in the serif.
cook: Cook mode: each step comes up into the light from below as it appears, the step text and counts are in the serif at large sizes, the wake light is a small glowing sun, and the buttons are solstice's own.
timers: Timer cards are lit from their foot with the time in the serif. A timer that has run out has its sky reddened to ochre: foot line, wash and a warm glow, with one overbright flare when it arrives.
quantity: The number field is a well lit from its foot (amber line, brighter while focused); the number is in the serif; the minus and plus are solstice's own buttons.
checklist: Rows are in the serif; the row under the pointer has the sun risen under it; a ticked item is struck through with a rust line and sinks. A group that is done shows a small sun in its count; empty and failed states keep the list's size.
tri: Included is the sun (☀ in an amber ring), left out is the moon (☾ in a red ring with the word struck through); either way is a hollow ring. Pointing lights the chip's foot in amber.
code: The code block is a plate lit from its foot with a warmed head; the title is in the serif, JSON keys are amber, and a failed read reddens the body's foot.
command: A terminal lit from its foot: the prompt at the start of every line is the sun's amber, the head is warmed, the copy button is solstice's own and confirms in words.
command-long: Long commands wrap or scroll inside the terminal; the continuation lines keep the prompt's width so the text never runs under it.
command-phone: The command at phone width: the head wraps, the code scrolls inside its plate and nothing touches the edge.
compare: The divider is the horizon, a glowing amber line, and the handle is the sun standing on it; the labels are small plates lit from their foot in the serif. A failed pane reddens its foot and keeps a normal-size Retry.
compare-live: The live compare slider: dragging moves the horizon and the sun; the picture panes keep their size while loading, with the busy card (the sun on its arc) over them.
